label: copy phase: fed-back consonant (p/g/t/k/r/j) input while outputting a consonant, early in the copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step, and never at recall_idx 0. The main driver is the fed-back input token: p and g give about 10x lift and together hold about 65% of activation mass, followed by t, k, r, j. Those six inputs cover 98% of activations (99% of mass), but precision is only 0.12. The token being output also matters: outputs j/g/t/k/r/e/p/y are favoured, and adding that condition roughly doubles precision. Activity peaks at recall_idx 2-3 (prev2 = <DEL>, 38% of mass) and fades later in the copy. The strongest activations are p (or g) fed back at recall_idx 1-2 in short sequences. It is nearly silent on digit and vowel inputs. It behaves like an additive mix of input-token, output-token and position preferences, so a boolean predicate reaches only about 0.43 F1.
